The human plateau began to shift. Posts flew through feeds like wildfire: it was prime time, right before the end of the workday. The viewer count instantly jumped from two hundred thousand to two hundred and fifty. Online media bots picked up on the event and started churning out news items about the provocative stream of "the most innovative business coach of our generation." And a woman, no less!

Now three hundred and fifty thousand people from all over the world were watching, liking, sharing, and paying real dollars to ask Freya a question. Three hundred and sixty. Three hundred and seventy. Every new thousand took Freya's breath away. And then came the time to answer.

The main thing was not to let this interaction with her followers turn into a collective Tinder date.

*"Do you have kids?"* a stranger asked. *"How do you achieve success when you have four of them?"*

Freya wanted to reply: *"You don't."* But, for one thing, moms on maternity leave made up forty-eight percent of her audience, so it was a sore subject. And for another, you couldn't give an answer like that to a follower who had most likely scraped together those fifty bucks from money she should have given her kids for school lunches. So Freya fell back on a polite, pre-rehearsed response.

"Everyone defines success for themselves," she said. "If you've always dreamed of being a mom or a dad, then your children *are* your capital. The key is to stick to an investment strategy and not hand your capital over to unverified funds."

*"Are you married?"* someone asked, donating the minimum five dollars.

By now Freya was leaving questions like that unanswered. Fortunately, a flood of more interesting (and pricier!) questions was flushing all the cheap provocations straight down the toilet.

Besides, her joke had landed. The chat was thrilled, and the viewer count kept climbing: a clip of her answer had already gone viral on Twitter. But with fame comes responsibility—the questions took a sharp turn into the genre of a collective Tinder date.
